items.title: Interview with a Mountain Guide
items.tvi: Phỏng vấn người dẫn đường leo núi
lines: Today I'm talking to Vu, who has guided climbers on Fansipan for over fifteen years. Vu, what's changed most in that time?

Definitely the number of visitors. When I started, we'd see maybe ten people a day on the trail. Since the cable car opened, thousands go to the top every day, though most of them never actually walk.
Has that been good for guides like you?

It's mixed. Fewer people hire guides for the full climb, because they can get to the summit in twenty minutes. On the other hand, the ones who do choose to walk are usually serious hikers, and they're often more interested in the forest and the local villages.
What's the biggest mistake inexperienced climbers make?

Underestimating the weather. It can be sunny at the bottom and freezing at the top, with thick fog that comes in very quickly. People turn up in trainers and a T-shirt, and that's genuinely dangerous.
And what keeps you doing the job after all these years?
Honestly, it's the moment when someone who thought they couldn't make it reaches the top. You see their face change. That never gets boring.

qs.q: What does Vu say about most cable car visitors?
qs.a: They don't walk any part of the mountain

qs.q: According to Vu, what is the most common mistake?
qs.a: Not preparing for changes in the weather

qs.q: What does Vu enjoy most about his job?
qs.a: Seeing people succeed when they doubted themselves

items.title: A Talk on Sleep and Memory
items.tvi: Bài nói về giấc ngủ và trí nhớ
items.text: A lot of students think that staying up all night before an exam is a sensible strategy. After all, more hours of study should mean more knowledge, right? Unfortunately, the research suggests the opposite. While we sleep, particularly during the deep stages early in the night, the brain replays and strengthens what we learned during the day, moving it from short-term into long-term memory. In one experiment, students who learned a list of words and then slept remembered around twenty percent more the next day than those who stayed awake for the same period. What's more, a lack of sleep reduces our ability to concentrate and to think flexibly, which is exactly what we need in an exam. So, if you have to choose between an extra two hours of revision at midnight and two hours of sleep, the sleep is very likely to be the better investment. The best approach, of course, is to spread your revision over several weeks, so that you never face that choice in the first place.

qs.q: What happens to learning during deep sleep?
qs.a: The brain strengthens it into long-term memory

qs.q: What did the experiment show?
qs.a: Students who slept remembered more words
w: Students who stayed awake learned faster
There was no difference between the groups

qs.q: What does the speaker recommend most?
qs.a: Studying regularly over several weeks

items.title: Two Friends Discuss a Film
items.tvi: Hai người bạn bàn về một bộ phim
lines: So, what did you think of it?
Honestly, I was a bit disappointed. Everyone had told me it was the best film of the year.
Really? I thought it was brilliant. The acting was incredible, especially the old fisherman.
Oh, I agree the acting was great. My problem was the story. It was so slow in the middle. Nothing happened for about forty minutes.
But that was the point, wasn't it? It was showing how boring and lonely his life had become after his wife died.
Maybe, but I don't need to be bored to understand that someone is bored.
Fair enough. What about the ending, though? I didn't see it coming at all.
No, the ending was clever, I'll give you that. I just wish they'd cut half an hour from the middle.
Well, I'm going to see it again next week. Maybe you should come and give it a second chance.
I'll think about it. But you're paying for the popcorn.

qs.q: What did both friends like?
qs.a: The acting

qs.q: Why does the woman think the middle was slow?
qs.a: To show the character's loneliness
w: Because the director made a mistake

qs.q: How does the man feel about seeing it again?
qs.a: He isn't sure yet

items.title: A News Report on Electric Motorbikes
items.tvi: Bản tin về xe máy điện
items.text: Sales of electric motorbikes rose by more than forty percent last year, according to figures released this morning by the national transport association. The increase has been strongest in large cities, where several local governments now offer discounts of up to three million dong to residents who exchange an old petrol motorbike for an electric model. Supporters say the shift could significantly reduce air pollution, which regularly reaches dangerous levels in winter. However, the association warns that the country still lacks enough public charging stations, particularly in apartment buildings, where many residents have no private space to charge their vehicles. There are also concerns about what will happen to the millions of batteries that will need to be replaced in the coming years. A spokesperson for the Ministry of Environment said that new rules on battery recycling would be announced before the end of the year.

qs.q: What do some local governments offer?
qs.a: Money off when people swap an old petrol bike

qs.q: What problem do apartment residents face?
qs.a: They have nowhere to charge their bikes
w: Electric bikes are banned in their buildings

qs.q: What will the Ministry of Environment do?
qs.a: Announce rules on recycling batteries

items.title: A Job Discussion
lines: I hear you've been offered the manager's job in Singapore. Congratulations!
Thanks, but I'm not sure I'm going to accept it.
Why not? It's a huge step up, and the salary must be much better.
It is. But my parents are getting older, and my father hasn't been well. If I move, I'll only be able to visit a couple of times a year.
That's a real worry. Could you ask the company for a shorter contract, maybe two years instead of five?
I did, actually. They said two years is too short to set up the new office properly. They offered three.
And what does your wife think?
She's keen. She'd love the chance to live abroad. That's what makes it so hard.
Well, whatever you decide, don't rush it. When do you have to give them an answer?
By the end of next week. I'm going to talk to my parents this weekend and see how they really feel.

qs.q: What is the man's main concern about the job?
qs.a: Being far away from his parents

qs.q: What did the company offer after he asked?
qs.a: A three-year contract

qs.q: What will he do this weekend?
qs.a: Talk to his parents

items.title: A Lecture on Coffee in Vietnam
items.tvi: Bài giảng về cà phê ở Việt Nam
items.text: Most people are surprised to learn that Vietnam is the world's second-largest coffee producer, after Brazil. Coffee was introduced by French missionaries in the nineteenth century, but production only really took off in the 1990s, when economic reforms allowed farmers in the Central Highlands to plant on a large scale. Today, the vast majority of Vietnamese coffee is robusta, a variety that is easier to grow and more resistant to disease than arabica, but which has a stronger, more bitter taste. For many years it was mainly used in instant coffee and cheaper blends sold abroad. Recently, however, a new generation of growers has started focusing on quality rather than quantity, producing speciality robusta that is winning international awards. At the same time, coffee farmers face serious challenges. Rising temperatures and irregular rainfall are already reducing yields, and some experts predict that large areas of the Highlands may become unsuitable for coffee within the next few decades.

qs.q: When did coffee production grow rapidly in Vietnam?
qs.a: In the 1990s

qs.q: Why do farmers grow robusta?
qs.a: It is easier to grow and resists disease
w: It sells for a higher price

qs.q: What threat to coffee farming is mentioned?
qs.a: Climate change

items.title: Complaining about a Delivery
items.tvi: Phàn nàn về đơn giao hàng
lines: Hello, I'm calling about an order I received yesterday. Order number five-five-eight-one.
Let me look that up. A bookshelf, delivered on Tuesday. Is there a problem?
Yes. Two of the shelves are cracked, and one of the screws is missing, so I can't put it together.
I'm very sorry about that. Did you notice the damage when the driver delivered it?
No, the box looked fine from the outside. I only saw it when I opened it in the evening.
I understand. We can either send replacement shelves and the screw, which would take about three days, or collect the whole thing and give you a full refund.
I'd rather have the replacement parts. I actually like the bookshelf, and I don't want to wait for a new one.
Of course. Could you email us a photo of the cracked shelves? Once we receive it, we'll send the parts immediately and give you a ten percent discount on your next order.
That sounds fair. I'll send the photo this afternoon.

qs.q: Why can't the caller build the bookshelf?
qs.a: Some shelves are cracked and a screw is missing

qs.q: What option does the caller choose?
qs.a: Replacement parts

qs.q: What must the caller do next?
qs.a: Send a photo of the damage

items.title: A Talk on Learning Languages
items.tvi: Bài nói về học ngoại ngữ
items.text: When people ask me how I learned five languages, they usually expect me to reveal some kind of secret method. The truth is rather less exciting. The most important thing I did was to make the language part of my daily routine, even for just twenty minutes, rather than studying for four hours once a week. Little and often beats long and rare, because the brain needs repeated contact to remember. The second thing was to stop being afraid of mistakes. For years I barely spoke Spanish, because I was waiting until I could speak it perfectly. It was only when I moved to Mexico and had no choice that I really improved. And finally, I chose materials I actually enjoyed: films, podcasts about football, cookery programmes. If you're bored, you'll give up, no matter how good the textbook is. None of this is magic, but it works.

qs.q: What does the speaker say about study time?
qs.a: Short daily practice is better than long rare sessions
w: Four hours a week is ideal

qs.q: What stopped the speaker improving in Spanish at first?
qs.a: Fear of making mistakes

qs.q: Why did the speaker choose enjoyable materials?
qs.a: Being bored makes people give up

items.title: Planning a Charity Event
items.tvi: Lên kế hoạch sự kiện từ thiện
lines: OK, so we need to decide on the event for the children's hospital. Any ideas?
Last year's concert raised quite a lot, but it was really expensive to organise. We spent nearly half the money on renting the hall and the sound system.
True. What about a sponsored run instead? People ask friends and family to pay them for each kilometre.
I like that. The costs would be much lower, and it's healthy too. But we'd need permission from the city to use the roads.
We could do it in the park instead. It's big enough for a five-kilometre route, and we wouldn't need to close any roads.
Good point. And maybe we could have a shorter route for children and older people, say one kilometre.
Great idea. Then whole families could take part. I'll contact the park office tomorrow.
And I'll design a poster. Shall we aim for the end of March, before it gets too hot?

qs.q: What was the problem with last year's concert?
qs.a: It cost a lot to organise

qs.q: Why do they choose the park?
qs.a: They won't need to close roads

qs.q: Why will there be a one-kilometre route?
qs.a: So children and older people can join

items.title: A Podcast about Minimalism
items.tvi: Podcast về lối sống tối giản
items.text: Two years ago, I owned over two thousand things. I know that because I counted them, which tells you something about how bored I was during the lockdown. I decided to try living with just one hundred items for a year. Of course, I had to make some rules: things like furniture and kitchen equipment that I shared with my partner didn't count. The first month was hard. I kept thinking I needed things I'd given away, especially books. But gradually I noticed that I spent less time cleaning, less time deciding what to wear, and a lot less money. What surprised me most was that I didn't feel I'd lost anything important. Now that the year is over, I've added a few things back, mainly books, but I'm still at about two hundred items. I'm not saying everyone should do this. But it made me realise how much of what I owned was just habit, not need.

qs.q: Why did the speaker count their possessions?
qs.a: They were bored during the lockdown

qs.q: What did the speaker miss most at first?
qs.a: Books

qs.q: What did the experiment teach the speaker?
qs.a: Many things they owned were not really needed
w: Living with less is very expensive

items.title: An Interview with a Night Nurse
items.tvi: Phỏng vấn một y tá làm ca đêm
lines: You've worked night shifts at the hospital for eight years. Do you ever get used to it?

Honestly, no. People think your body adjusts, but I still feel jet-lagged for a day or two after a run of nights. What changes is that you learn to manage it. I sleep in a completely dark room, I don't drink coffee after two in the morning, and I'm very strict about protecting my sleep, even if it means missing family events.

It is. My children are used to me sleeping during the day, but I did miss a lot of school plays when they were young. On the other hand, nights have their advantages. There are fewer staff, so you have more responsibility, and you get to know your patients differently. People often want to talk at three in the morning, when they can't sleep and they're worried.
Would you go back to day shifts?
Probably, eventually. But not yet. I think I'd miss the calm and the sense that the ward depends on you.

qs.q: What does the nurse say about getting used to night work?
qs.a: Her body has never fully adjusted
w: It takes about a year to adjust
She adjusted after the first few weeks

qs.q: Why does she mention school plays?
qs.a: To show what she has sacrificed because of her job
w: To show how proud she is of her children
To explain why she chose night shifts

qs.q: What advantage of night shifts does she describe?
qs.a: Patients are more willing to talk

qs.q: How does she feel about returning to day shifts?
qs.a: She expects to do it one day but is not ready yet
w: She would like to change immediately

items.title: A Radio Report on Food Delivery Apps
items.tvi: Phóng sự về ứng dụng giao đồ ăn
items.text: Over the past five years, food delivery apps have changed the way millions of people in Vietnamese cities eat. For customers, the attraction is obvious: a huge choice of dishes, delivered in under half an hour, often with discounts. For restaurants, however, the picture is more complicated. Many owners we spoke to said the apps had brought them new customers, especially young office workers, but that the commission they pay, often around a quarter of each order, makes it hard to earn a profit. Some have responded by raising prices on the app while keeping them lower for customers who eat in. Drivers, too, have mixed feelings. They value the flexibility of choosing their own hours, but several told us that their income has fallen as more drivers have joined, and that bad weather and traffic make long shifts exhausting. Meanwhile, environmental groups are concerned about the amount of plastic packaging used for deliveries. One app has started letting customers refuse plastic cutlery, which it says has saved millions of forks and spoons. Critics say that's a welcome step, but only a small one.

qs.q: According to the report, what problem do restaurants face with the apps?
qs.a: The commission reduces their profits

qs.q: How have some restaurants responded?
qs.a: By charging more on the app than in the restaurant

qs.q: Why has drivers' income fallen, according to some drivers?
qs.a: There are more drivers competing for orders
w: The apps have cut their pay rates

qs.q: What is the critics' view of the plan to reduce plastic cutlery?
qs.a: It is positive but not enough

items.title: Two Colleagues Discuss a Presentation
items.tvi: Hai đồng nghiệp bàn về bài thuyết trình
lines: So how do you think the presentation went this morning?
The content was fine, I think. The figures were clear. But I'm not sure the clients were convinced.
Well, nobody asked any questions at the end. With this client, silence is usually a bad sign. When they're interested, they argue about everything.
Maybe they just needed time to think. It was a lot of information.
Possibly. But I also think we spent too long on the technical details and not enough on what they'd actually gain. That's what they care about.
That's fair. So what do we do now? Send them a follow-up?
Yes, but a short one. One page, focusing on the cost savings, and an offer to come back and answer questions. If we send another thirty slides, they'll never read it.
Agreed. I'll draft it tonight and you can check it in the morning.

qs.q: Why does the woman think the clients were not convinced?
qs.a: They did not ask any questions

qs.q: What does the woman say this client usually does when interested?
qs.a: They argue a lot

qs.q: What mistake does the woman think they made?
qs.a: They focused too much on technical details

qs.q: What kind of follow-up do they agree to send?
qs.a: A brief document about the benefits
w: A longer presentation with more slides

items.title: A Museum Guide on a Famous Painting
items.tvi: Hướng dẫn viên bảo tàng nói về một bức tranh
items.text: If you'd like to gather round, this is probably the most famous painting in the museum, and also the one that people most often misunderstand. At first glance, it looks like a peaceful scene: a family having lunch by a river on a sunny day. Many visitors stop for a moment, think how charming it is and walk on. But look more closely at the faces. Nobody is smiling, and nobody is looking at anyone else. The father is staring at a newspaper, the mother is looking at the river, and the children seem to be in their own worlds. The painting was completed in 1938, just before the war, and many historians believe the artist was trying to show a family, and perhaps a country, that was together but no longer connected. The bright colours were a deliberate choice: they make the sense of isolation even stronger, because it is hidden behind such a pleasant surface. Interestingly, when it was first exhibited, critics described it as cheerful. It was only decades later that people began to read it differently.

qs.q: What does the guide say about the painting?
qs.a: It is often misunderstood

qs.q: What detail does the guide draw attention to?
qs.a: The people are not interacting with each other
w: The river is painted very darkly
The family is eating very little

qs.q: Why, according to the guide, did the artist use bright colours?
qs.a: To make the feeling of isolation stronger
w: Because the painting was for a café
To show that the family was happy

qs.q: What does the guide say about the critics in 1938?
qs.a: They saw the painting as happy
w: They understood its true meaning immediately

items.title: Advice on Starting to Run
items.tvi: Lời khuyên khi bắt đầu chạy bộ
lines: I've decided to start running, but every time I try, I give up after a week. Any advice?
The most common mistake is doing too much too soon. People go out, run as fast as they can for twenty minutes, feel terrible and decide running isn't for them.

Then try the opposite. For the first few weeks, mix running and walking: run for one minute, walk for two, and repeat that about eight times. You should be able to talk while you're running. If you can't, you're going too fast.
That's the point. You want to finish each run feeling you could have done a bit more. That's what makes you come back. Increase the running time gradually, maybe by a minute a week.
And what about shoes? Do I need expensive ones?
Not necessarily expensive, but they should fit properly. Go to a proper running shop if you can, and avoid running in old trainers. That's how a lot of beginners get injured.

qs.q: What does the man say is the most common mistake beginners make?
qs.a: Starting too hard
w: Choosing the wrong time of day

qs.q: How can a runner tell if they are going too fast?
qs.a: They cannot speak while running

qs.q: Why does the man want beginners to finish feeling they could do more?
qs.a: It encourages them to continue
w: It helps them run faster immediately

qs.q: What is the man's attitude to running shoes?
qs.a: They must fit well but need not be very expensive
w: Any old trainers are fine for beginners
